preview: Keisha Gupte shares her Wells Fargo internship interview experience, detailing the online assessment, technical rounds involving DSA and OOPs, and final selection.
content: WELLS FARGO INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE KEISHA GUPTE | TY BTECH IT Coding / Online Assessment Round: This round was conducted on AMCAT platform on 8th of August, 2022. The webcam had to be kept on, also no changing tabs/windows was allowed. It consisted of three sections- 1) Verbal Aptitude: It had questions on grammar, such as choosing the right tense, or choosing the most appropriate word according to its definition. It had comprehension questions too. It was pretty easy 2) Business Aptitude: A company’s graph of their growth was given and there were follow up questions on that, such as analysing or interpreting its data. There was a time crunch while solving these questions. I couldn’t solve all of them and marked the answers of the remaining questions randomly as there was no negative marking 3) Coding Section: This section had 2 questions. I don’t remember the questions specifically because there was a huge gap between our coding round and interview round. Both were array-based questions and the difficulty level was easy. I was able to pass 10/10 test cases for one question and 10/13 test cases for the other question Interview round: This round was conducted on the 7th of September. 7 students were shortlisted for this round. A day before the interview, we were asked to submit our resumes. Technical + HR interview First round: All the candidates were given different zoom links and our first interview was at 9.30am. I had joined the link 5 mins prior to the given time. The interviewer asked me to give a brief introduction about myself. You can mention about your projects, describe your contribution in it, and what all achievements you have had so far. Do mention your hobbies too. I was given two problems to solve. I had to predict the next element of the following series: 80, 10, 70, 15, 60, ?. Another similar question on completing a series was asked. Be careful about what you include in your resume because they keep it open all the time and ask questions based on what you have written in it. I had included Java, C++, and Python as the languages that I was proficient in. I was asked the difference between these languages and which one I preferred and why. Next, I was asked to explain the OOPs concepts and give examples etc. I was also asked to explain various data structures, how I had used these data structures and to give a real-world example for each Also, remember to keep the screenshots of the company’s presentation. Or you can do a little research about the company before the interview. Basically, you must be a little aware of the company’s various sectors and policies. I was asked to tell him what I knew about Wells Fargo. This round went well and all the 7 candidates were chosen for the next round. Second Interview Round: This round was scheduled at 12.40pm. The interviewer asked me to give the most optimal way of finding out if a number is prime number. Next, I was asked to write a query such that the duplicate tuples of the table were to be deleted and only one entry of these tuples was to be kept in the table. It was a typical interview question and required using row id column. I gave it a try but wasn’t able to answer it correctly. https://www.oracletutorial.com/advanced-oracle-sql/how-to-delete-duplicate-records-in-oracle/ Next, he gave a scenario where I was to design a product for a customer. I had to explain the steps involved and how I would approach it. I answered that by giving the basic steps such as planning, designing, adding required functionalities, testing, deploying etc. His feedback was that the first thing to do is market research and understand the requirements of the customer. A few more HR questions related to Wells Fargo were asked which I don’t remember exactly. The name of the shortlisted candidates came at around 5. I was luckily shortlisted along with 3 other candidates! • I wasn’t asked any questions on OS but be prepared for anything as it solely depends on what the interviewer wishes to ask • Be prepared to be asked thorough questions on everything written in your resume • Also, be ready with a few questions related to the company FOR DSA: • I followed GFG Practice problems. And for DP I watched Aditya Verma’s playlist FOR OS AND DBMS: • I followed interview bit questions for last minute revision and referred to the notes I had made • You can also refer to Apna College notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KV-9I5D6iddJbAoDzPEBVR6izf-j_7PXq3JQSC7KC2Q/edit https://drive.google.com/file/d/1B_kmekdghu-sO8-eXZ1kc4Xx_YtB8BPM/view FOR OOPS: • I followed interview bit questions for last minute preparation and had referred Love Babbar’s Cheat Sheet https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/ https://whimsical.com/object-oriented-programming-cheatsheet-by-love-babbar-YbSgLatbWQ4R5paV7EgqFw ALL THE BEST!!!!!
